::: {#rem-quantifier-order}
#### Order of quantifiers

Read nested quantifiers from left to right.
In $\forall s, \exists c, E(s, c)$,
the course $c$ is chosen after the student $s$, so it may depend on $s$.
In $\exists c, \forall s, E(s, c)$,
one course $c$ must work for every student.

Swapping two quantifiers of the same kind does not change the meaning:
$\forall x, \forall y, P(x, y)$ means the same as $\forall y, \forall x, P(x, y)$,
and likewise for $\exists$.
Swapping a $\forall$ and an $\exists$ can change it,
as parts 1 and 2 of @exr-enrollment show.

:::
